questions.q: Who bought Black Beauty after Jerry?
choices: A corn dealer and baker
A cab owner named Skinner
A farmer from the country
A lady with a carriage
questions.evidence: I was sold to a corn dealer and baker

questions.q: Who was to blame for Black Beauty's heavy loads?
choices: The foreman, who was always hurrying everyone
Jakes the carter, who enjoyed being cruel
The baker's children, who rode on top of the loads
The lady who lived at the top of the hill
questions.evidence: there was a foreman who was always hurrying and driving every one

questions.q: What made it hard for Black Beauty to pull easily?
choices: The check-rein held his head up
His new shoes were much too tight
The cart had a broken wheel
He was not given enough to eat
questions.evidence: always had the check-rein up, which prevented me from drawing easily

questions.q: How did Black Beauty feel when he was whipped while doing his very best?
choices: It took the heart out of him
He felt proud of how hard he worked
He did not mind it at all
He became angry and kicked the cart
questions.evidence: it took the heart out of me

questions.q: What did the lady ask Jakes to do?
choices: Take the check-rein off and give the horse his head
Whip the horse harder until he reached the top
Unload the whole cart and carry the sacks up
Go and find a stronger horse to help pull
questions.evidence: Quite down, give him his head altogether

questions.q: What happened after the rein was taken off and Jakes spoke kindly?
choices: Black Beauty pulled the load steadily up the hill
Black Beauty bolted and ran away down the road
The cart tipped over and spilled the sacks
Jakes sold the horse to the kind lady right there and then
questions.evidence: I pulled it steadily up the hill

questions.q: Why did Jakes want to put the check-rein back on?
choices: The other carters would laugh at him; it was the fashion
It made the horse go faster on the flat roads
The lady had told him to put it back on
The horse liked it and held his head proudly
questions.evidence: I should be the laughing-stock of all the carters; it is the fashion

questions.q: What did the lady say about animals being called "dumb"?
choices: They cannot say how they feel, but suffer just as much
They do not feel pain the way people do at all
They are not clever enough to understand what is done to them
They should never be used for hard work
questions.evidence: they do not suffer less because they have no words

questions.q: What problem did the badly-lighted stable cause Black Beauty?
choices: It weakened his eyes, so daylight hurt them
It made him too cold to sleep at night
It made him lose his appetite for oats
It made his coat dull and fall out in patches
questions.evidence: it very much weakened my sight
